transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I've been having a really hard time at work lately because during long meetings and when I'm out on the job site, my mind just keeps drifting. I can't seem to stay focused on what people are saying to me or keep track of what I'm supposed to be monitoring.
Have you also been feeling down or anxious, or are these focus problems happening even when you're not stressed or sad?

I don't really feel depressed or anxious, just incredibly stressed about my current work situation. I'm not sure about the connection, but these focus problems have actually been happening since I was a kid, long before this current stress started.
When did you first notice these focus problems—was it during childhood, and did they affect school or other activities back then?

Yes, they definitely go back to childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly sending notes home about me daydreaming in class and talking over the other kids. I also could never finish my worksheets unless someone was standing right over me to keep me on track.

The early onset and persistent pattern of inattention, distractibility, and failure to complete tasks despite external supervision strongly support F90.0 (hyperkinetic disorder). The absence of significant mood or anxiety symptoms reduces the likelihood of affective or anxiety disorders. Therefore, the current candidate is limited to F90.0.
